title: Generalized Priority-Aware Shapley Value
claim: Sampler mixing time scales polynomially with problem size, staying near the ideal rate on simple structures but approaching the worst-case bound on general ones.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, log-log plots, shared legends, reference bound lines
description: Two side-by-side log-log line plots share the y-axis label 'Mixing Time' and the x-axis variable n, which runs from 4 to about 22. The left panel is titled 'DAG' and the right panel 'General Graph'. Each panel shows colored lines for four settings: weak or strong λ crossed with weak or strong ω, in blue, purple, green and red. Solid lines are a greedy variant and dashed lines are a random variant. Two black reference lines mark an ideal n² rate (solid) and an upper bound of (4/π²) n³ log n (dashed). In the DAG panel the curves mostly sit between the two bounds, and the greedy blue and green curves fall near or below the n² line. In the General Graph panel the dashed curves rise toward the cubic bound. Legends sit inside the plot areas. The eye goes first to the black reference lines and the rising colored curves.
caption: Illustration of priority structures. Dashed arrows in (b): [ref] require special precedence structures.
abstract: Shapley value and its priority-aware extensions are widely used for valuation in machine learning, but existing methods require pairwise priority to be binary and acyclic, a restriction spectacularly violated in real-data examples such as aggregated human preferences and multi-criterion comparisons. We introduce the generalized priority-aware Shapley value (GPASV), a random order value defined on arbitrary directed weighted priority graphs, in which pairwise edges penalize rather than forbid order violations. GPASV covers a range of classical models as boundary cases. We establish GPASV through an axiomatic characterization, develop the associated computational methods, and introduce a priority sweeping diagnostic extending PASV's. We apply GPASV to LLM ensemble valuation on the cyclic Chatbot Arena preference graph, illustrating that priority-aware valuation is not a one-button operation: different balances of pairwise graph priority versus individual soft priority produce substantively different valuations of the same data.
